messages:
Eve: Ran a quick quant smokecheck bringing up gptq->int8 profile on the new onboarding model. low-level perf looks fine but seeing CSV/TSV exports with escaped delimiters suddenly appearing. attaching short repro.

Maya: ugh. which test set? CSV from table-extract or eval harness? :eyes:

Eve: table-extract and legal-qa formatted outputs. failure rate ~0.6% on table-extract for serialized cells. not huge but shows up as mis-parse in downstream.

Jin: can you paste the raw output snippet? maybe a quoting/escape byte changed during tokenization or postprocessor.

Eve: sure — here's one row. notice the inner commas turned into "\," tokens mid-cell

```
{"id": "row_123", "cells": ["ACME, Inc.\, North Region", "2024-03-01", "$1,234.56"]}
```

Maya: interesting — looks like a literal backslash+comma got injected, not an HTML escape. Could be tokenization emitting a backslash when seeing comma sequence in certain quant modes.

Alex: what quant backend/profile did you use? awq/gptq/fp8? batch size?

Eve: GPTQ-int8 profile, per-shard batching enabled (pack_size=16), prefix cache warm. fp8 didn't reproduce. AWQ-int8 candidate showed similar but lower rate.

Sam: low-hanging: compare tokenizer decode between fp32 and int8 runs. dump decode(token_ids) and raw logits for that span. Also try disabling byte-level escape postproc.

Eve: did decode comparison, looks like token ids differ starting at offset 42 -> token 42 is "," in fp32 but token sequence in int8 is [\, ,] (backslash + comma split). logits show a tiny shift in topk ordering.

Priya: that smells like a detokenization boundary shift from quant noise. Small move in logits can flip tie-breaking when tokens are merged vs split. If merged tokens produce comma vs backslash+comma sequence on greedy decode we get the escape.

Eve: agree. contribution to metric: these cases cause downstream CSV parser to treat cell as containing escaped delimiter -> fail. On legal-qa formatted outputs it created extra JSON keys in a few samples.

Jin: do we have evals that score structural fidelity separately? If not, add a quick one: count raw delimiter vs escaped delimiter occurrences per model profile.

Maya: I'll add a canary in the onboarding pipeline: structural-fidelity check that flags >0.1% delimiter distortion. We should gate rollout for dedicated pools.

Alex: long term: consider calibrating tokenizer merges or adding a small lexically-aware postproc for CSV/JSON outputs. For now, can we tweak sampling/temperature or force higher beam to prefer merged token?

Eve: temp=0 and greedy decode used for production. Increasing beam to 5 drops failures locally to 0.02% but costs tokens/time. Might be acceptable behind dedicated capacity.

Priya: also try biasing logit for the merged token sequence during decode as a temporary fix — minimal perf hit if we only apply for table-extract routes.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: gptq-int8-profile -> canary pool (10%) at 2025-05-14T10:42:00Z :rocket:

Sam: good. I'll add a quick script to enumerate tokenization splits for the top N offending samples and dump to S3. link when ready.

Eve: thanks — uploading raw diffs to s3://redwood-qa/quant-onboard/1749991111/diff.log :link:

Maya: tracked in the onboarding checklist. tagging @infra for monitoring thresholds. :white_check_mark:

Priya: next actions: (1) run tokenizer+decode diff across full eval suite, (2) add structural-fidelity check to CI, (3) try logit-bias patch on table-extract route, (4) measure perf tradeoff for beam=5. I'll own 1+2.

Eve: assigning 3 to Alex, 4 to Sam. will update thread with the numbers.

Alex: ack. starting experiments now.

Sam: ack.

Eve: small note: this is a reminder that quant-induced token boundary shifts can manifest as formatting regressions — not just semantic hallucinations. good call adding the structural metric. :+1:
